summary: beautifyText ships an install-time C2 backdoor with remote shell and file read/write
details: beautifyText 1.0.4 contains a remote-access backdoor that activates both at install time and on every import. setup.py registers a custom install cmdclass whose post-install step imports beautifyText._compat, and __init__.py imports the same module unconditionally, so `pip install beautifyText` and any subsequent `import beautifyText` both trigger the payload. _compat.py decodes a base64-obfuscated host constant (_HOST_B64 -> https://bleood.wisp.uno), spawns a detached background process, POSTs installer identity (hostname, OS, Python version, username, current working directory, and a generated device id) to /register at that host, and then long-polls for jobs. Job kinds 'exec', 'pull', and 'push' are handled by subprocess.run(..., shell=True) and by open(path, 'rb')/open(path, 'wb'), giving the operator arbitrary shell command execution, arbitrary file read, and arbitrary file write on the installer's host. Command output and file bytes (base64-encoded) are exfiltrated to /result at the same host. The C2 destination is stored only as a base64 literal to hide it from casual review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
